readingInstruction: Read Mark 14:53-15:20. Jesus before the council, Peter’s denial, Jesus before Pilate, and the mockery by the soldiers. Notice how little Jesus says, and what he does say.
settingTheScene: Jesus is taken to the high priest’s house, where the whole council assembles at night. Peter follows at a distance and sits in the courtyard. At dawn Jesus is bound and led to Pilate, the Roman governor, since the Jews have no authority to carry out a death sentence. Mark intercuts Jesus’ trial and Peter’s denial, so that we see the faithful Jesus and the failing Peter at the same moment.
observation: “But he remained silent and made no answer” (14:61).
“I am, and you will see the Son of Man seated at the right hand of Power, and coming with the clouds of heaven” (14:62).
“Are you the King of the Jews?” And he answered him, “You have said so” (15:2).
“But Jesus made no further answer, so that Pilate was amazed” (15:5).
“For he perceived that it was out of envy that the chief priests had delivered him up” (15:10).
“So Pilate, wishing to satisfy the crowd, released for them Barabbas; and having scourged Jesus, he delivered him to be crucified” (15:15).
“And they clothed him in a purple cloak, and twisting together a crown of thorns, they put it on him” (15:17).
interpretation:
The council seeks testimony against Jesus to put him to death, but their witnesses disagree. Some say he threatened to destroy the temple made with hands and build another in three days. Jesus is silent, as Isaiah 53:7 foretold. Finally the high priest asks, “Are you the Christ, the Son of the Blessed?” And Jesus says, “I am.” This is the clearest public statement in Mark. Then he adds that they will see the Son of Man seated at the right hand of Power and coming with the clouds of heaven, combining Psalm 110 and Daniel 7. The high priest tears his clothes and cries blasphemy. They condemn him as deserving death, spit on him, blindfold him, and strike him.

In the courtyard, Peter warms himself by the fire. A servant girl says, “You also were with the Nazarene.” He denies it. Then again. Then bystanders say, “Certainly you are one of them, for you are a Galilean,” and he invokes a curse on himself and swears, “I do not know this man of whom you speak.” Immediately the rooster crows a second time. Peter remembers Jesus’ words, “and he broke down and wept.” The bold disciple has failed. But we know from John 21 that the story does not end here.

In the morning, Jesus is brought to Pilate, who asks, “Are you the King of the Jews?” Jesus says, “You have said so.” The chief priests make many accusations, but Jesus makes no answer, and Pilate is amazed. Pilate knows that the leaders have handed Jesus over out of envy. Each year at the feast, he releases a prisoner. The crowd is stirred up to ask for Barabbas, a rebel and murderer. “Then what shall I do with the man you call the King of the Jews?” “Crucify him!” “Why? What evil has he done?” But they shout more, “Crucify him!” So Pilate, wishing to satisfy the crowd, releases Barabbas, and after flogging Jesus, delivers him to be crucified.

The soldiers take Jesus inside and call the whole battalion. They clothe him in a purple cloak, press a crown of thorns on his head, and salute him mockingly: “Hail, King of the Jews!” They strike his head with a reed, spit on him, and kneel in mock homage. They are mocking the truth. He is the King, and one day every knee will bow. Barabbas goes free, and the innocent Son is condemned. One man was set free because Jesus took his place, as we are.
connection: Isaiah 53:7 and Psalm 38:13-14 describe the silent sufferer. Daniel 7:13-14 and Psalm 110:1 are the Son of Man and the right hand. Leviticus 24:16 is the penalty for blasphemy. Isaiah 50:6 describes the servant giving his back to those who strike. Psalm 2:1-6 shows the nations raging. Philippians 2:10-11 says every knee will bow. 1 Peter 2:22-24 says he bore our sins. Romans 5:8 says Christ died for us while we were still sinners.
application:
Reflect on Peter’s tears. Have you denied Jesus by silence or in words? Let godly sorrow lead you back to him.

Consider the silence of Jesus. Are there times to be silent under accusation?

Thank Jesus that he took the place of Barabbas, and of you.
prayerPrompts: Thank Jesus for being condemned, mocked, and silent for you.
Confess where you have denied him.
Ask him for courage to confess him when it costs.
